sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马斯。

sentences.en: For over a decade now, listeners of this show have heard me say that we're headquartered in beautiful downtown, or now uptown, Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 十多年来，本节目的听众一直听我说，我们的总部位于美丽的奥克兰市中心，或者现在是上城区，加利福尼亚州。

sentences.en: These days, the 99% Invisible team is spread all across the U.S.
sentences.zh: 如今，《99%隐形》团队遍布美国各地。

sentences.en: and Canada.
sentences.zh: 还有加拿大。

sentences.en: Hey, Chris.
sentences.zh: 嘿，克里斯。

sentences.en: But a few of us still live and work in Oakland.
sentences.zh: 但我们中仍有一些人住在奥克兰并在这里工作。

sentences.en: And despite how far flung the 99PI team is, there's just something about the city that feels like the spiritual home of our show.
sentences.zh: 尽管《99%隐形》团队分布广泛，但这座城市总有一种感觉，就像是我们节目的精神家园。

sentences.en: I think what makes Oakland home for me is this incredible diversity of, like, peoples and places that are all sort of contained within it.
sentences.zh: 我认为奥克兰之所以让我感到像家，是因为它内部蕴含着令人难以置信的多样性，比如各种各样的人和地方。

sentences.en: This is Alexis Madrigal, an Oakland resident himself and one of the hosts of the local public radio call-in show Forum on KQED.
sentences.zh: 这位是亚历克西斯·马德里加尔，他本人就是奥克兰居民，也是KQED当地公共广播访谈节目《论坛》的主持人之一。
zh_words: 亚历克西斯·马德里加尔

sentences.en: He also happens to be a longtime friend of mine.
sentences.zh: 他恰好也是我的老朋友。

sentences.en: And when I first moved here, you know, 12, 13 years ago, it was kind of like a quarter of the population was white, a quarter of the population was black, a quarter was Latino,
sentences.zh: 当我刚搬到这里时，你知道，大概12、13年前，人口构成大概是四分之一白人，四分之一黑人，四分之一拉丁裔，

sentences.en: and like a quarter was Asian.
sentences.zh: 还有四分之一是亚裔。

sentences.en: You know, there's tons of working class people, there's tons of non-working class people, and they're all kind of shoved into the same place,
sentences.zh: 你知道，这里有大量的工薪阶层，也有大量的非工薪阶层，他们都被挤在同一个地方，

sentences.en: right in view of this kind of glittering future city of San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 就在那座闪闪发光的未来之城旧金山的视野之内。

sentences.en: And we're kind of like the back lot, you know?
sentences.zh: 我们就像是后勤基地，你懂吗？

sentences.en: And I love that part of it always made me feel quite at home, and also it really helped me, like, fall in love with the city.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢那一部分，它总是让我感到宾至如归，也确实帮助我爱上了这座城市。

sentences.en: When you cross the Bay Bridge from San Francisco to Oakland, you don't see some flashy skyline.
sentences.zh: 当你从旧金山穿过海湾大桥来到奥克兰时，你看到的不是什么华丽的天际线。

sentences.en: Instead, your eye is either drawn up to the densely forested hills or down towards the port, where a series of rail lines, shipping containers,
sentences.zh: 相反，你的目光要么被吸引到森林茂密的山丘上，要么向下看向港口，那里有一连串的铁路线、集装箱，

sentences.en: and massive industrial cranes line the shore.
sentences.zh: 以及巨大的工业起重机排列在岸边。

sentences.en: The cranes have become the, like, official and unofficial symbol of the city.
sentences.zh: 这些起重机已经成为这座城市官方和非官方的象征。

sentences.en: People spray paint them around, like, people have them on shirts, like, it does represent us in some crucial way.
sentences.zh: 人们到处喷涂它们，人们把它们印在衬衫上，它确实以某种关键的方式代表了我们。

sentences.en: And in part, it's because any route into the city, basically, you end up seeing them.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，这是因为进入城市的任何路线，基本上你最终都会看到它们。

sentences.en: They are kind of our skyscrapers, right?
sentences.zh: 它们就像是我们的摩天大楼，对吧？

sentences.en: They are this thing which is out of scale with, like, human life.
sentences.zh: 它们是那种与人类生活不成比例的东西。

sentences.en: In the shadow of those cranes lies the neighborhood of West Oakland.
sentences.zh: 在这些起重机的阴影下，坐落着西奥克兰社区。

sentences.en: It's a predominantly black working-class community.
sentences.zh: 这是一个以黑人工薪阶层为主的社区。

sentences.en: And in Alexis's new book, The Pacific Circuit, he writes about how this neighborhood has been shaped by the global economic forces that connect Oakland to the rest of the world.
sentences.zh: 在亚历克西斯的新书《太平洋环路》中，他写到了这个社区是如何被连接奥克兰与世界其他地区的全球经济力量所塑造的。

sentences.en: Every year, billions of dollars' worth of stuff gets loaded into a container and onto a cargo ship destined for the port of Oakland.
sentences.zh: 每年，价值数十亿美元的货物被装进集装箱，装上开往奥克兰港的货船。

sentences.en: The supply chain that keeps goods flowing between Asia and the Bay Area has transformed life as we know it today.
sentences.zh: 维持亚洲和湾区之间货物往来的供应链已经改变了我们今天所知的生活。

sentences.en: Products are cheaper.
sentences.zh: 产品更便宜了。

sentences.en: They arrive at your door in a flash.
sentences.zh: 它们瞬间就能送到你家门口。

sentences.en: But all that has a coSt.
sentences.zh: 但这一切都是有代价的。

sentences.en: And in West Oakland, the impacts of global trade are felt by residents every day.
sentences.zh: 在西奥克兰，居民们每天都能感受到全球贸易的影响。

sentences.en: The story of this neighborhood and its relationship to the port next door tells us a lot about the trade-off cities have made in service of economic growth.
sentences.zh: 这个社区的故事及其与隔壁港口的关系，告诉了我们很多关于城市为了经济增长而做出的权衡。

sentences.en: It's also a place where people have had to learn how to push back against these enormous financial forces to save their neighborhood, their neighbors, and themselves.
sentences.zh: 这也是一个人们必须学会如何反抗这些巨大金融力量，以拯救他们的社区、邻居和他们自己的地方。

sentences.en: So, I was hoping that we could start off by going, like, way back.
sentences.zh: 所以，我希望我们能从很久以前开始谈起。

sentences.en: How far back do you want to go?
sentences.zh: 你想追溯到多远以前？

sentences.en: I think I can go all the way back if you want.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，我想我可以一直追溯到最初。

sentences.en: Let's kind of go all the way back.
sentences.zh: 让我们一直追溯到最初吧。

sentences.en: Like, maybe.
sentences.zh: 比如，也许。

sentences.en: Railroads.
sentences.zh: 铁路。

sentences.en: I mean, kind of.
sentences.zh: 我是说，差不多吧。

sentences.en: I mean, so talk to me about West Oakland.
sentences.zh: 我是说，跟我谈谈西奥克兰吧。

sentences.en: How did this part of this city end up becoming, like, the center of black life in the Bay Area?
sentences.zh: 这座城市的这一部分是如何最终成为湾区黑人生活中心的？

sentences.en: Yeah, so Oakland became the black center of the Bay Area basically because of the railroads, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，奥克兰之所以成为湾区的黑人中心，基本上是因为铁路，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, people quite famously know about, like, sort of the porters, and the porters had a union, and many of them were black.
sentences.zh: 我是说，人们非常清楚搬运工的事，搬运工有工会，而且他们中许多人是黑人。

sentences.en: And so, that was kind of mixed in with, like, all kinds of other folks who had come as, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，这与各种各样来到这里的人混在一起，你知道，

sentences.en: immigrants to West Oakland and specifically to sort of the very western part of West Oakland.
sentences.zh: 作为移民来到西奥克兰，特别是来到西奥克兰的最西部。

sentences.en: And just so people can orient themselves, this is the part that's, like, right on the bay.
sentences.zh: 为了让人们找准方位，这是紧靠海湾的那一部分。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，是的。

sentences.en: And right next to the port.
sentences.zh: 而且就在港口旁边。

sentences.en: Yeah, so over time, as more black people came, they just kind of, you know, in the way that many migrants do, ended up kind of clumping in this particular part of the city.
sentences.zh: 是的，随着时间的推移，越来越多的黑人来到这里，他们就像许多移民一样，最终聚集在城市的这个特定区域。

sentences.en: And, of course, there were racist restrictions, which got tighter later, but it kind of established the core, and then more and more people kind of came to that.
sentences.zh: 当然，当时有种族限制，后来变得更严了，但它建立了一个核心，然后越来越多的人来到这里。

sentences.en: And you started to see this kind of, you know, if you research other black areas in the West,
sentences.zh: 你开始看到这种，你知道，如果你研究西部的其他黑人地区，

sentences.en: people inevitably call a street with lots of black commercial activity the Harlem of the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 人们不可避免地会把一条有很多黑人商业活动的街道称为“西部的哈莱姆”。

sentences.en: And so, it became one of these Harlem's of the West along 7th Street in West Oakland.
sentences.zh: 所以，它成为了西奥克兰第七街沿线的“西部的哈莱姆”之一。

sentences.en: And what that meant was there were places where you could get oftentimes southern food because most of the people who were coming up were from the south.
sentences.zh: 这意味着那里有你可以经常吃到南方食物的地方，因为大多数来到这里的人都来自南方。

sentences.en: So, you could get ribs and you could get things that you maybe wouldn't find in the rest of the Oakland area.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以吃到排骨，还可以吃到你在奥克兰其他地区可能找不到的东西。

sentences.en: And music and bars and there were unions and there were just kind of an integrated whole of black life took place really right there along 7th Street in West Oakland.
sentences.zh: 还有音乐和酒吧，有工会，西奥克兰第七街沿线确实发生了一个完整的黑人生活整体。

sentences.en: Which then, of course, as more and more black migrants came, especially to work in the shipyards of World War II, that made that part of town into like a very dense,
sentences.zh: 当然，随着越来越多的黑人移民到来，特别是在二战期间到造船厂工作，这使得城镇的那一部分变得非常密集，

sentences.en: both lovely and also very difficult place to live as well.
sentences.zh: 既可爱又是一个生活起来非常困难的地方。

sentences.en: Because it was right in the industrial grime, as intended by city planners at the time.
sentences.zh: 因为它就在工业污垢之中，正如当时的城市规划者所预期的那样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, let's talk about that.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们来谈谈那个吧。

sentences.en: Like, how did Oakland city planners in the early part of the 20th century segregate, divide, and zone black residents into some of the roughest parts of the city?
sentences.zh: 比如，20世纪初的奥克兰城市规划者是如何将黑人居民隔离、划分并规划到城市最艰苦的地区去的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, I have Shattuck, who was the sort of planning engineer in Oakland during this sort of early New Deal period in which, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，我有沙特克，他是新政早期奥克兰的规划工程师，当时，你知道，

sentences.en: the federal government was running all of these kinds of research programs
sentences.zh: 联邦政府正在开展各种各样的研究项目，

sentences.en: to understand the housing stock and populations inside cities.
sentences.zh: 以了解城市内部的住房存量和人口。

sentences.en: And part of that task was assembling all of this data on every block in basically urban America.
sentences.zh: 这项任务的一部分是收集美国城市中每个街区的所有数据。

sentences.en: And what they ended up finding in Oakland was that you could sort of segregate off the area where black people lived,
sentences.zh: 他们在奥克兰最终发现的是，你可以把黑人居住的区域隔离出来，

sentences.en: intermixed with some white people of various like ethnic groups, from the area that was still mostly white.
sentences.zh: 与各种族裔的白人混居，与仍然主要是白人的区域隔开。

sentences.en: And what they end up recommending is essentially a freeway to cut off the black population and hem them against the sort of industrial shoreline.
sentences.zh: 他们最终建议的是修建一条高速公路，切断黑人人口，并将他们围困在工业海岸线附近。

sentences.en: And this is the freeway that was built in the 1950s that basically split West Oakland in half.
sentences.zh: 这就是20世纪50年代修建的高速公路，它基本上把西奥克兰一分为二。

sentences.en: I mean, today the neighborhood is still surrounded by highways.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，今天这个社区仍然被高速公路包围着。

sentences.en: But for a long time, one of those highways ran kind of right through the middle of the community.
sentences.zh: 但在很长一段时间里，其中一条高速公路就穿过了社区的中间。

sentences.en: And it pinned sort of the very western part of West Oakland right against the water.
sentences.zh: 它把西奥克兰的最西部紧紧地压在水边。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I think it's worth remembering for people that like, well, it might sound nice to live by the shoreline.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们值得记住的是，虽然住在岸边听起来可能不错，

sentences.en: You know, the industrial shoreline in this sort of pre-environmental regulations era was disgusting.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在环境法规出台之前的那个时代，工业海岸线是令人作呕的。

sentences.en: And so you had the railroads running through.
sentences.zh: 所以你有铁路穿过。

sentences.en: You had factories doing all kinds of stuff.
sentences.zh: 你有工厂在做各种各样的事情。

sentences.en: This is still an industrial city.
sentences.zh: 这仍然是一个工业城市。

sentences.en: And then you had, you know, that the water itself was toxic and there's sewer outflows and there's all kinds of stuff happening there.
sentences.zh: 然后你还有，你知道，水本身是有毒的，有污水排放，那里发生着各种各样的事情。

sentences.en: And so this is the one area of town where essentially Oakland city planners said, this is where black people can live and this is where black people must live.
sentences.zh: 所以这是城镇中奥克兰城市规划者基本上说“这是黑人可以居住的地方，这是黑人必须居住的地方”的唯一区域。

sentences.en: So black residents of Oakland were living right by the port.
sentences.zh: 所以奥克兰的黑人居民就住在港口旁边。

sentences.en: And around that time in the 1950s, the port was also seen as sort of revolution in the shipping industry with containerization.
sentences.zh: 大约在20世纪50年代，港口也被视为航运业的一场革命，即集装箱化。

sentences.en: And we've actually talked a lot about containerization on the show before with you, in fact.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们之前在节目中和你谈论过很多关于集装箱化的事情。

sentences.en: But basically, instead of moving a bunch of small individual boxes on and off of cargo ships, everything was going inside of this like one big box instead.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，不是在货船上搬运一堆小型的独立箱子，而是所有东西都装进这个大箱子里。

sentences.en: And those big boxes or containers would get dropped off in a yard nearby and a bunch of trucks would come by and take them away.
sentences.zh: 那些大箱子或集装箱会被卸在附近的堆场，然后一堆卡车会过来把它们运走。

sentences.en: But for this whole operation to work, you basically need a lot of land to store those containers on.
sentences.zh: 但为了让整个操作顺利进行，你基本上需要大量的土地来存放这些集装箱。

sentences.en: Absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: You need hundreds of acres of more or less useless land right on the coast of a major city.
sentences.zh: 你需要数百英亩位于大城市海岸边几乎没用的土地。

sentences.en: You know, it's like, and how do you find that?
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像是，你如何找到这些土地？

sentences.en: And basically the answer that the whole containerization trade came up with was to implant in poor neighborhoods in places adjacent to the big city.
sentences.zh: 基本上，整个集装箱贸易得出的答案是在大城市附近贫困社区的邻近地区进行植入。

sentences.en: So if you think about the first two big container ports, you have Newark, which of course is right, you know, outside New York City.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想想最初的两个大型集装箱港口，你有纽瓦克，当然就在纽约市外，

sentences.en: And you have Oakland.
sentences.zh: 还有奥克兰。

sentences.en: And so it was the plan, basically,
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上是奥克兰城市规划者的计划，

sentences.en: of Oakland City planners for as long as they had had dreams to push out the population of West Oakland so that Oakland's industrial base could take over that whole area.
sentences.zh: 只要他们有梦想，就会把西奥克兰的人口赶走，这样奥克兰的工业基础就可以接管整个区域。

sentences.en: Like they would call it like completely unfit for human habitation.
sentences.zh: 比如他们会称其为完全不适合人类居住。

sentences.en: Like when it was basically the densest residential neighborhood in the East Bay.
sentences.zh: 就像它基本上是东湾人口最密集的住宅区时那样。

sentences.en: So not only did Oakland City planners segregate this neighborhood with that highway, but they also tried to take over the area and redevelop it for more business down by the port.
sentences.zh: 所以奥克兰城市规划者不仅用那条高速公路隔离了这个社区，他们还试图接管该地区并为港口附近的更多商业进行重新开发。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean,
sentences.zh: 是的，我是说，

sentences.en: I think the the bargain essentially that the city of Oakland had been wanting to make since the early 1950s was to sacrifice that area as a residential place and the people in it for economic growth at the port.
sentences.zh: 我认为奥克兰市自20世纪50年代初以来一直想做的交易，本质上就是牺牲那个区域作为居住地，牺牲那里的人民，以换取港口的经济增长。

sentences.en: And I think what I found deeply compelling about this particular story is like we've made that tradeoff with black people so many times where we're sort of like, yeah,
sentences.zh: 我认为我发现这个特定故事非常引人注目的地方在于，我们已经多次与黑人做过那种权衡，我们就像是，是的，

sentences.en: that's going to hurt some black people, but we're going to redevelop the city.
sentences.zh: 那会伤害一些黑人，但我们要重新开发这座城市。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And this is this is like such a pure example where people saw an economic opportunity and all that was standing in the way were some like black lives.
sentences.zh: 这是一个如此纯粹的例子，人们看到了经济机会，而挡在路上的只有一些黑人的生命。

sentences.en: The Port of Oakland started container operations in 1962 as the first container port on the West Coast of the United States.
sentences.zh: 奥克兰港于1962年开始集装箱作业，成为美国西海岸第一个集装箱港口。

sentences.en: It helped revolutionize global trade.
sentences.zh: 它帮助彻底改变了全球贸易。

sentences.en: Money started to pour into the Bay Area.
sentences.zh: 资金开始涌入湾区。

sentences.en: But in West Oakland, right next to this booming port, the remaining black residents were forced to live with increasing levels of pollution.
sentences.zh: 但在西奥克兰，就在这个繁荣的港口旁边，剩下的黑人居民被迫忍受日益严重的污染。

sentences.en: At the time, especially in 1960s, there is nowhere for black people to go.
sentences.zh: 当时，特别是在20世纪60年代，黑人无处可去。

sentences.en: There aren't places where they can live because of the racial restrictions that are placed across the whole country and also very strongly in the Bay Area.
sentences.zh: 由于全国范围内，特别是在湾区，存在着种族限制，他们没有可以居住的地方。

sentences.en: And so people are stuck just living with the sort of these incredible changes to the local economy,
sentences.zh: 所以人们只能忍受当地经济的这些惊人变化，

sentences.en: which involve tons of diesel trucks running these short routes that are called drayage, you know, in and out of ports and are kind of the oldest, dirtiest trucks that you can find.
sentences.zh: 其中包括大量的柴油卡车在港口内外进行短途运输，这被称为短途运输，你知道，它们是你所能找到的最古老、最脏的卡车。

sentences.en: And so what develops in West Oakland is a localized air quality problem that's really about diesel particulate matter.
sentences.zh: 所以西奥克兰出现的是一个局部空气质量问题，这实际上是关于柴油颗粒物的问题。

sentences.en: And diesel particulate matter is bad for people like it's it's bad for your lungs, increases your chance of asthma.
sentences.zh: 柴油颗粒物对人有害，因为它对你的肺不好，会增加你患哮喘的几率。

sentences.en: It does bad things to your brain.
sentences.zh: 它对你的大脑也有害。

sentences.en: I mean, there's like it is why people don't want to live in really polluted environments, more or less.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这就是为什么人们不想生活在污染严重的环境中的原因，或多或少是这样。

sentences.en: But if it's the only place you can live and this is the growing business of the city, you're kind of stuck.
sentences.zh: 但如果这是你唯一能住的地方，而这又是城市不断发展的业务，你就被困住了。

sentences.en: And so that that's what happened in West Oakland.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是西奥克兰发生的事情。

sentences.en: One of the first activist groups to try to grapple with everything happening down by the port were the Black Panthers.
sentences.zh: 最早试图解决港口发生的一切的活动组织之一是黑豹党。

sentences.en: The group's headquarters were in West Oakland, so they witnessed firsthand how all these changes affected Black residents in the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 该组织的总部就在西奥克兰，所以他们亲眼目睹了所有这些变化是如何影响社区黑人居民的。

sentences.en: Prior to containerization, the port had been a place where Black people could find work.
sentences.zh: 在集装箱化之前，港口一直是黑人可以找到工作的地方。

sentences.en: But containerization required less manpower.
sentences.zh: 但集装箱化需要的人力更少。

sentences.en: So now the port was both polluting the neighborhood and taking jobs away from its people.
sentences.zh: 所以现在港口既污染了社区，又夺走了人们的工作。

sentences.en: The Panthers were very up on the idea that containerization was transforming Oakland.
sentences.zh: 黑豹党非常清楚集装箱化正在改变奥克兰的想法。

sentences.en: And Huey Newton, you know, who's kind of lead theorist of the Panthers, he writes this essay called The Technology Question,
sentences.zh: 休伊·牛顿，你知道，他是黑豹党的主要理论家，他写了一篇名为《技术问题》的文章，

sentences.en: which I think is just it's so ahead of its time and kind of thinking about why global supply chains are important.
sentences.zh: 我认为这非常超前，并且在某种程度上思考了为什么全球供应链很重要。

sentences.en: And one of the things that he says basically is like people like the shit that capitalism produces.
sentences.zh: 他基本上说的一件事是，人们喜欢资本主义生产的那些东西。

sentences.en: And that is the trickiest component of it.
sentences.zh: 而这是其中最棘手的部分。

sentences.en: Like we all like this stuff that comes out of this system that we don't like.
sentences.zh: 我们都喜欢这个我们不喜欢的系统所产生的东西。

sentences.en: And so what do we do about it?
sentences.zh: 那么我们该怎么办？

sentences.en: And I think I would say the Panthers never really answered that question, but neither have we.
sentences.zh: 我想我会说黑豹党从未真正回答过这个问题，但我们也没有。

sentences.en: I think all of us who are living in our modern world are like, God, I don't like all this stuff that is happening.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们所有生活在现代世界的人都觉得，天哪，我不喜欢正在发生的所有这些事情。

sentences.en: I don't like this system.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢这个系统。

sentences.en: I don't like what it does to people.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢它对人们所做的事情。

sentences.en: I don't like what it does to workers.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢它对工人所做的事情。

sentences.en: I don't like what it does to environment.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢它对环境所做的事情。

sentences.en: But I do have the latest iPhone and I have this computer and I have all the things.
sentences.zh: 但我确实有最新的iPhone，我有这台电脑，我有所有的东西。

sentences.en: I have an electric car and you know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 我有一辆电动汽车，你明白我的意思吗？

sentences.en: And I think we've never really been able to tackle that thing, but they were maybe the first to like just pinpoint it so precisely.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们从未真正能够解决那个问题，但他们可能是第一个如此精确地指出它的人。

sentences.en: After the break, one resident of West Oakland takes on the global supply chain.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，一位西奥克兰居民将挑战全球供应链。

sentences.en: And we are back with Alexis Madrigal and we're talking about his new book, The Pacific Circuit.
sentences.zh: 我们回到了亚历克西斯·马德里加尔身边，我们正在谈论他的新书《太平洋环路》。
zh_words: 亚历克西斯·马德里加尔

sentences.en: So, Alexis, in the first part of our chat, we talked about how starting in the 1950s,
sentences.zh: 所以，亚历克西斯，在我们谈话的第一部分，我们谈到了从20世纪50年代开始，

sentences.en: West Oakland was segregated by this highway that ran down through the middle of the neighborhood, which, by the way,
sentences.zh: 西奥克兰被这条穿过社区中间的高速公路隔开了，顺便说一句，

sentences.en: was adding to the pollution of the neighborhood in its own right.
sentences.zh: 它本身就在加剧社区的污染。

sentences.en: And then this boom next door at the port comes along and adds even more to the problem.
sentences.zh: 然后隔壁港口的繁荣随之而来，使问题变得更加严重。

sentences.en: But you write about how in 1989, there's this random, tragic, but also transformational event that happens in Oakland.
sentences.zh: 但你在书中写到，1989 年奥克兰发生了一起随机的、悲剧性的，同时也具有变革意义的事件。

sentences.en: Yeah, so there's kind of a real before and after in West Oakland, which is this freeway going down because of the 1989 earthquake.
sentences.zh: 没错，西奥克兰在那之后确实有了明显的分水岭，因为 1989 年的地震导致了高速公路的坍塌。

sentences.en: That is the Cypress section of the Nimitz Freeway.
sentences.zh: 那就是尼米兹高速公路的赛普拉斯路段。

sentences.en: And you can see, oh, my God, look at that.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到，天哪，看看那个场景。

sentences.en: The freeway has just completely collapsed.
sentences.zh: 高速公路完全坍塌了。

sentences.en: And it comes down in this, like, deus ex machina kind of way in the sense that the earthquake knocks it down.
sentences.zh: 它就像“机械降神”一样，因为地震把它震塌了。

sentences.en: It would have never come down otherwise, right?
sentences.zh: 否则它永远不会倒塌，对吧？

sentences.en: There's no way that anyone was going to take down this, like, connector route.
sentences.zh: 根本没人会去拆除这条连接线。

sentences.en: But it comes down and suddenly it changes the possibilities of the entire neighborhood, you know.
sentences.zh: 但它倒塌了，突然间改变了整个社区的可能性，你知道的。

sentences.en: And, of course, that change has to be managed and all these things have to happen.
sentences.zh: 当然，这种变化需要被妥善管理，很多事情也随之发生。

sentences.en: But it was just like the way that overnight this structural feature,
sentences.zh: 但那种感觉就像是，一夜之间，这个结构性特征——

sentences.en: which has its roots all the way back in the baldly racist suggestion of segregating black people in the west part of West Oakland, it just comes down one day.
sentences.zh: 它根植于那种赤裸裸的种族主义建议，即在西奥克兰的西部隔离黑人——就这样在某一天消失了。

sentences.en: And the rest of the neighborhood's history henceforth, minus that piece of urban infrastructure, is just different.
sentences.zh: 而此后该社区的历史，在去掉了那块城市基础设施后，就变得完全不同了。

sentences.en: I mean, you talk about this in your book, like, people who have basically grown up in a literal shadow of a highway and they never heard birds because there was no nature around.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你在书中谈到过，那些基本上是在高速公路的阴影下长大的人，他们从未听过鸟叫，因为周围根本没有自然环境。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, on day one, they see light.
sentences.zh: 而突然之间，在第一天，他们看到了光。

sentences.en: They see the sky.
sentences.zh: 他们看到了天空。

sentences.en: They hear birds.
sentences.zh: 他们听到了鸟鸣。

sentences.en: It's really something.
sentences.zh: 这真的很了不起。

sentences.en: So this highway comes down.
sentences.zh: 所以这条高速公路倒塌了。

sentences.en: And the immediate physical effect is that there's a lot more light and less pollution in West Oakland.
sentences.zh: 直接的物理影响是西奥克兰的光照多了很多，污染少了。

sentences.en: But the second, less tangible effect is that this highway is gone and it feels to some people like, wow, we have this opportunity.
sentences.zh: 但第二个不太明显的效应是，高速公路消失了，对一些人来说，感觉就像是，哇，我们有了机会。

sentences.en: Like, some things that might have felt fixed might not be so permanent after all.
sentences.zh: 就像有些看似固定的东西，可能终究并非不可改变。

sentences.en: And that spirit of change is really embodied by one person in your book.
sentences.zh: 而这种变革精神在你的书中由一个人体现了出来。

sentences.en: So let's introduce everyone to Miss Margaret Gordon.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们向大家介绍玛格丽特·戈登女士。

sentences.en: Oh, Miss Margaret Gordon.
sentences.zh: 噢，玛格丽特·戈登女士。

sentences.en: I didn't actually think I was initially going to have a central character in the way that Miss Margaret became.
sentences.zh: 起初我并没有想过要有一个像玛格丽特女士后来那样的核心人物。

sentences.en: But she would go around telling people, before I had decided this at all, she'd be like, he's writing a book about me.
sentences.zh: 但在我还没决定之前，她就会到处跟人说：“他正在写一本关于我的书。”

sentences.en: And I'd be like, well, you know, Miss Margaret, I just want to know, I'm not sure it's like about you per se, but, you know, I, you know.
sentences.zh: 我会说：“嗯，你知道，玛格丽特女士，我只是想了解情况，我不确定这是否算是一本关于你的书，但是，你知道……”

sentences.en: And she's like, he's writing a book about me.
sentences.zh: 而她会说：“他正在写一本关于我的书。”

sentences.en: And eventually it turned out to be more or less what happened.
sentences.zh: 最终结果也确实差不多是这样。

sentences.en: And one reason is I realized an alternate title for this book was Everybody Knows Miss Margaret.
sentences.zh: 其中一个原因是，我意识到这本书的另一个标题可以是《人人都认识玛格丽特女士》。

sentences.en: Like, she connected up all these different kinds of people because of her work out at the port, but also because of her longtime connections in the community.
sentences.zh: 她通过在港口的工作，以及她在社区长期的联系，把各种各样的人连接在了一起。

sentences.en: It just represented so much of that kind of mid-century boomer black experience in the Bay where, you know,
sentences.zh: 她代表了湾区那一代黑人经历的很多方面，你知道的，

sentences.en: somebody's encounters with the state are both like voluminous and they have lots of them and many of them are quite negative.
sentences.zh: 一个人与政府的接触既频繁又繁杂，而且很多时候都是相当负面的。

sentences.en: And yet what emerges out of that is someone with an incredible read on governmental action and an incredible read on sort of how to work within the constraints of a system that more or less wants to exclude you as,
sentences.zh: 然而，从中涌现出来的是一个对政府行为有深刻见解的人，一个非常懂得如何在系统限制内运作的人，尽管这个系统或多或少想要排斥你，作为一个——

sentences.en: you know, a poor black woman in a neighborhood that's not represented very well.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一个贫穷的黑人女性，生活在一个代表性不足的社区里。

sentences.en: You mentioned Miss Margaret's connections with the port and to the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 你提到了玛格丽特女士与港口以及社区的联系。

sentences.en: And in your book, you write about how in the 90s she started to get active in the community around this air quality problem.
sentences.zh: 在你的书中，你写到她在 90 年代开始围绕空气质量问题在社区变得活跃起来。

sentences.en: Could you tell me more about that?
sentences.zh: 你能多跟我讲讲那个吗？

sentences.en: I mean, she was at that time kind of struggling with one of her kids and was, you know, trying to be an advocate in the school system.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当时她正为一个孩子的问题而挣扎，试图在学校系统中为孩子争取权益。

sentences.en: And then she'd go into the schools in West Oakland and like, you know, the nurse would have like a big, you know, basket of inhalers labeled with all the kids' names.
sentences.zh: 然后她走进西奥克兰的学校，护士那里有一个大篮子，里面装满了贴着孩子们名字的吸入器。

sentences.en: And she'd be like, well, why is it that like all these kids have asthma?
sentences.zh: 她会问：“为什么这些孩子都有哮喘？”

sentences.en: And when you say the kids had asthma, you mean there was really an asthma crisis.
sentences.zh: 当你提到孩子们患有哮喘时，你是说当时真的存在一场哮喘危机。

sentences.en: Like at the time, some studies showed that asthma rates in West Oakland were like seven times the state average.
sentences.zh: 当时的一些研究显示，西奥克兰的哮喘发病率是全州平均水平的七倍左右。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So for a long time in West Oakland, people knew that the air wasn't good.
sentences.zh: 所以长期以来，西奥克兰的人们都知道空气质量不好。

sentences.en: But of course, there's cumulative impacts of all this stuff over time.
sentences.zh: 但当然，随着时间的推移，所有这些因素都有累积影响。

sentences.en: There's just the increase in truck traffic that occurred over time.
sentences.zh: 卡车交通量随着时间推移而增加。

sentences.en: And because it was a neighborhood that was essentially sacrificed for the economic growth of the region, it was really treated like, you know.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个本质上为了地区经济增长而被牺牲的社区，它真的被当作……你知道的那样对待。

sentences.en: And so what ends up happening is that Miss Margaret, along with some other folks, want to get like a handle on like, well, what's happening in this neighborhood?
sentences.zh: 所以最终发生的是，玛格丽特女士和其他一些人想要弄清楚，这个社区到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: Like the city does not have good visibility into like how this neighborhood works or what it needs.
sentences.zh: 市政府对这个社区的运作方式或需求缺乏清晰的了解。

sentences.en: And so they join up together to create this thing that's eventually called the West Oakland Environmental Indicators Project.
sentences.zh: 于是他们联合起来创建了一个项目，最终被称为“西奥克兰环境指标项目”。

sentences.en: And that environmental indicators is sort of what they were first after.
sentences.zh: 而“环境指标”正是他们最初追求的目标。

sentences.en: They basically did survey work.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上做了调查工作。

sentences.en: They counted trucks.
sentences.zh: 他们统计了卡车数量。

sentences.en: They looked at government data sources.
sentences.zh: 他们查阅了政府数据来源。

sentences.en: And they create this essentially set of indicators that says, like, these are the things that are bad in our neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 他们创建了一套本质上的指标，说明：这些是我们社区糟糕的地方。

sentences.en: These are the things that are good.
sentences.zh: 这些是好的地方。

sentences.en: Here's our strengths.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的优势。

sentences.en: We want to change these things.
sentences.zh: 我们想要改变这些东西。

sentences.en: And it became clear pretty much right away that it was really about the trucks.
sentences.zh: 很快就很清楚，问题确实出在卡车上。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And you have this stat in your book that West Oakland had like thousands of truck trips going through the neighborhood every day.
sentences.zh: 你在书中提到一个统计数据，西奥克兰每天有数千次卡车往返穿过社区。

sentences.en: Because, I mean, at the time, so much of the economy was tied to this port.
sentences.zh: 因为当时，很大一部分经济都与这个港口挂钩。

sentences.en: So the number of things going in and out of this neighborhood is kind of unimaginable.
sentences.zh: 所以进出这个社区的东西数量多到难以想象。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And so the trucks were just like making a mess all over the neighborhood, cracking sidewalks, idling outside your door and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以卡车在社区里到处制造混乱，压坏人行道，在你家门口怠速排放等等。

sentences.en: And, of course, the pollution itself, which was obvious to everyone who was living there and was as a direct consequence was harming the health of the children in the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有污染本身，这对住在那里的人来说显而易见，并且直接导致了社区儿童的健康受损。

sentences.en: And so that group essentially becomes the key environmental justice pressure group in West Oakland saying to the city, saying to the port of Oakland,
sentences.zh: 所以那个组织本质上成为了西奥克兰关键的环境正义压力团体，对市政府、对奥克兰港口说：

sentences.en: holding their feet to the fire, you must do something.
sentences.zh: 给他们施加压力，你们必须做点什么。

sentences.en: Like, you cannot assume our bad health in your plans.
sentences.zh: 你们不能在计划中默认我们的健康状况恶化。

sentences.en: You must account for cleaning up the air and this place even as you want the economy to grow in the area.
sentences.zh: 即使你们想要发展地区经济，也必须考虑到净化空气和这个地方。

sentences.en: So not too long after launch of this group,
sentences.zh: 所以在这个组织成立后不久，

sentences.en: Margaret Gordon moves from community activists into another role where she really had some say over what happens down at the port and she becomes a port commissioner.
sentences.zh: 玛格丽特·戈登从社区活动家转变为另一个角色，在那里她对港口发生的事情有了发言权，她成为了一名港口专员。

sentences.en: And so can you tell me about the significance of her getting appointed to that position?
sentences.zh: 那么你能告诉我她被任命为该职位的意义吗？

sentences.en: You know, for West Oakland, there had never been a community representative like on this port board, which is just having such a big impact on their lives.
sentences.zh: 对于西奥克兰来说，港口董事会里从来没有过社区代表，而这个董事会对他们的生活影响巨大。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But no one from the community was actually ever there.
sentences.zh: 但社区里从来没有人真正在那里。

sentences.en: It was always like real estate developers and, you know, business people, kind of the elite of the city.
sentences.zh: 那里总是房地产开发商和商界人士，某种程度上是城市的精英。

sentences.en: So to have someone from the area who lives right on 7th Street, who's been dealing with all those impacts on the port, which is a huge deal for West Oakland.
sentences.zh: 所以能有一位来自该地区、就住在第七街、一直应对港口所有影响的人，这对西奥克兰来说是一件大事。

sentences.en: And I think for Margaret, it really was the high point of her career in terms of having, you know, institutional power, power that could be wielded.
sentences.zh: 我认为对玛格丽特来说，这确实是她职业生涯的巅峰，就拥有制度性权力而言，一种可以被行使的权力。

sentences.en: And she used it to help get this maritime air quality improvement plan instituted.
sentences.zh: 她利用这种权力帮助制定了“海事空气质量改善计划”。

sentences.en: And this was like her plan to rein in emissions from the port.
sentences.zh: 这就是她用来控制港口排放的计划。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, what that actually has translated into over the years as the changes and reforms that they made have rolled out was that emissions from diesel particulates.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，随着他们所做的变革和改革的实施，多年来这实际上转化为柴油颗粒物排放的下降。

sentences.en: So that's, you know, a lot, most of the stuff coming out of the trucks fell 98 percent, at least by by some measures.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，卡车排放的大部分东西减少了 98%，至少根据某些衡量标准是这样。

sentences.en: And overall, emissions in the neighborhood fell by a lot.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，社区的排放量大幅下降。

sentences.en: I mean, huge improvement in air quality.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，空气质量有了巨大的改善。

sentences.en: And I really do think even the port itself traces it to this maritime air quality improvement plan, which was sort of Margaret's crowning achievement.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为连港口本身都将其归功于这个海事空气质量改善计划，这算是玛格丽特的巅峰成就。

sentences.en: So I just think, you know, it's one of those things that feels so important, even though it was just, you know, one person getting onto a board.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是认为，你知道，这是一件感觉如此重要的事情，尽管它只是一个人进入了董事会。

sentences.en: But that person made an impact because they knew things about what were happening at the neighborhood level that other people didn't.
sentences.zh: 但那个人产生了影响，因为她了解社区层面发生的事情，而其他人并不了解。

sentences.en: Today, it's clear that Miss Margaret Gordon has done a ton to improve the air quality in West Oakland.
sentences.zh: 今天，很明显玛格丽特·戈登女士为改善西奥克兰的空气质量做了大量工作。

sentences.en: But clean air isn't the only thing her neighborhood needs,
sentences.zh: 但清洁空气并不是她社区唯一需要的东西，

sentences.en: because the same racist city planning that put a highway through the middle of the town and trapped black residents next to the port also deprived West Oakland of economic opportunities.
sentences.zh: 因为同样的种族主义城市规划，在城镇中间修建了一条高速公路，并将黑人居民困在港口旁边，也剥夺了西奥克兰的经济机会。

sentences.en: And those two things, the need for clean air and the need for jobs, can be hard to balance in a place like Oakland.
sentences.zh: 而这两件事，对清洁空气的需求和对就业的需求，在奥克兰这样的地方很难平衡。

sentences.en: There's a story in Alexis's book that really illustrates this dynamic, and it has to do with the battle over a decommissioned army base down by the port.
sentences.zh: 亚历克西斯的书中有一个故事很好地说明了这种动态，它与港口附近一个已退役的陆军基地的争夺战有关。

sentences.en: The dispute pits a hotshot local developer, Phil Tagami, up against Miss Margaret.
sentences.zh: 这场纠纷让当地炙手可热的开发商菲尔·塔加米与玛格丽特女士对立起来。

sentences.en: Tagami's plan wants to use the land the old army base sits on to expand the port and create more jobs.
sentences.zh: 塔加米的计划想要利用旧陆军基地的土地来扩建港口并创造更多就业机会。

sentences.en: Miss Margaret wants a plan that benefits her community too, but she, understandably, after years of fighting for clean air, has some concerns.
sentences.zh: 玛格丽特女士也想要一个造福社区的计划，但她在多年为清洁空气而战后，理所当然地有一些担忧。

sentences.en: It's such an interesting situation, what happened out there, because you essentially have two figures in my mind who really are Oakland people.
sentences.zh: 那里的情况非常有趣，因为在我看来，你本质上拥有两个真正属于奥克兰的人物。

sentences.en: Like, they're deep in the Oakland community.
sentences.zh: 他们深深扎根于奥克兰社区。

sentences.en: Both of them have these super deep roots, but they're so different.
sentences.zh: 他们两人都有着极其深厚的根基，但他们却如此不同。

sentences.en: They're just so, so different.
sentences.zh: 他们真的太、太不同了。

sentences.en: You know, Miss Margaret, environmental justice leader, West Oakland.
sentences.zh: 你知道，玛格丽特女士，西奥克兰的环境正义领袖。

sentences.en: And then you have kind of Phil Tagami, who's this kind of downtown developer, but who himself, like, didn't go to college,
sentences.zh: 然后是菲尔·塔加米，他是一个市中心的开发商，但他自己没有上过大学，

sentences.en: worked his way up as a developer doing ticky tech stuff into eventually being the guy who redid the Fox Theater, you know, one of these old beautiful theaters, which is now,
sentences.zh: 作为一名开发商，通过做一些小项目起家，最终成为重修福克斯剧院的人，你知道，这是那些古老美丽的剧院之一，现在是——

sentences.en: you know, this amazing music venue in downtown Oakland.
sentences.zh: 你知道，奥克兰市中心一个很棒的音乐场所。

sentences.en: And then he locks his jaws onto this project of the army base and essentially cuts what's really quite an innovative deal at the time with a lot of labor groups and stuff where they got a huge percentage of local hire.
sentences.zh: 然后他锁定了陆军基地的这个项目，并与许多劳工团体达成了一项在当时相当创新的协议，他们获得了很大比例的本地雇佣。

sentences.en: So, you know, people from near the project area would get would get hired.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，项目附近的人会被雇佣。

sentences.en: They agreed to a whole bunch of stuff that the labor groups of Oakland and the East Bay really wanted.
sentences.zh: 他们同意了奥克兰和东湾劳工团体真正想要的一大堆事情。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But there was still this kind of environmental thorn in the side.
sentences.zh: 但仍然存在一种环境上的眼中钉。

sentences.en: And it felt to Miss Margaret that that kind of got brushed aside in the rush to deliver these jobs in the sort of like post-financial crisis years, you know, into Oakland,
sentences.zh: 对玛格丽特女士来说，在金融危机后的几年里，为了提供这些就业机会，这种担忧似乎被匆忙地搁置了，你知道，进入奥克兰，

sentences.en: where I don't know if people remember, but there was a good paying jobs was like one of those kind of catchphrases of the Obama era.
sentences.zh: 我不知道人们是否还记得，但“高薪工作”是奥巴马时代的口号之一。

sentences.en: And, you know, that's what this was delivering.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这就是它所带来的。

sentences.en: And the whole local power structure was behind it.
sentences.zh: 整个当地权力结构都在支持它。

sentences.en: They were behind Tagami doing all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们支持塔加米做所有这些事情。

sentences.en: And Margaret kind of got pushed to the side and her environmental concerns were sort of, you know, swept under the rug.
sentences.zh: 玛格丽特被推到了一边，她的环境担忧被扫到了地毯下。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this all came to a head with one particular issue,
sentences.zh: 这一切在一个特定的问题上达到了顶峰，

sentences.en: because one of the things that was discovered that would be on the table for shipping through this newly expanded port was coal.
sentences.zh: 因为人们发现，通过这个新扩建的港口运输的货物中，将包括煤炭。

sentences.en: Dun, dun, dun, dun.
sentences.zh: 当当当当。

sentences.en: Yeah, right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: It's like the Sierra Club's got their new national headquarters in Oakland.
sentences.zh: 就像塞拉俱乐部在奥克兰设立了新的全国总部一样。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: It's like the most anti-Trump place, a major city in the country.
sentences.zh: 这就像是全国主要城市中最反特朗普的地方。

sentences.en: I think we went in 2016, I think we went 96 percent against Trump.
sentences.zh: 我想我们在 2016 年，我想我们有 96% 的人反对特朗普。

sentences.en: It's pretty similar this time.
sentences.zh: 这次也差不多。

sentences.en: You know, this is like the anti- like you cannot imagine a place, I think, that would be less amenable to wanting to have coal be like part of our local economy.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就像是反……我想你无法想象一个更不愿意让煤炭成为我们当地经济一部分的地方。

sentences.en: And so this export terminal would essentially have run coal cars right through right through West Oakland.
sentences.zh: 所以这个出口码头本质上会把煤炭列车直接穿过西奥克兰。

sentences.en: So people were very, they were big mad and there were all these city council meetings and there's all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以人们非常、非常愤怒，举行了所有的市议会会议，还有所有这些事情。

sentences.en: It's one of those moments in a city's history where you just realize like, oh, man, like what can a city do?
sentences.zh: 这是城市历史中让你意识到的一刻，就像，天哪，一个城市能做什么？

sentences.en: Like if a city can't stop this, which the entire city is opposed to, then like what does that say about power in our modern world?
sentences.zh: 如果一个城市无法阻止这一点，而整个城市都反对它，那么这说明了我们现代世界的权力是什么？

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And it's also like this is all that global trade economy trying to plow its way through West Oakland again.
sentences.zh: 而且这就像是全球贸易经济再次试图在西奥克兰横冲直撞。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And basically what Oakland has tried to do is like file multiple lawsuits against the developer,
sentences.zh: 基本上奥克兰试图做的是对开发商提起多项诉讼，

sentences.en: but they keep losing because the contract Agami has with the city basically says that he can do it, that he can ship the coal if he wants to.
sentences.zh: 但他们一直输，因为塔加米与城市签订的合同基本上说他可以这样做，如果他想的话，他可以运输煤炭。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, litigation after litigation, you know, just by delaying it, you're kind of waging like siege financial warfare.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，诉讼接连不断，你知道，仅仅通过拖延，你就是在进行一种围困式的金融战。

sentences.en: And so to this day, you know, as we're recording here, it still doesn't exist as a coal export terminal.
sentences.zh: 所以直到今天，在我们录制的时候，它仍然不存在作为一个煤炭出口码头。

sentences.en: Like it doesn't, it's not there, you know, and it's the fight continues all these years on.
sentences.zh: 它不存在，它不在那里，你知道，这场斗争在这些年后仍在继续。

sentences.en: And at least for me, what I find so interesting about this whole fight over the army base is just how these things have a tendency to grind everything to a halt.
sentences.zh: 至少对我来说，关于陆军基地的这场斗争，我发现最有趣的是这些事情往往会使一切陷入停滞。

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，

sentences.en: it's been more than 25 years since the old army base was decommissioned and still neither the city nor the developer have figured out how to use this piece of land to benefit the city.
sentences.zh: 旧陆军基地退役已经超过 25 年了，但无论是城市还是开发商，都还没有想出如何利用这块土地来造福城市。

sentences.en: And, you know, don't get me wrong, like I don't want it to be a coal terminal either.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，别误会我，我不希望它成为煤炭码头，

sentences.en: Like I think that idea sucks, but I would love it if the city would build something because between the housing crisis and the climate crisis and everything else,
sentences.zh: 我觉得那个主意很烂，但我希望城市能建造一些东西，因为在住房危机、气候危机和其他一切之间，

sentences.en: we are going to need to build things and build them pretty faSt.
sentences.zh: 我们需要建造东西，而且要很快地建造。

sentences.en: You know, I sometimes, because we know we have to rebuild so much infrastructure for climate change,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我有时，因为我们知道我们必须为气候变化重建如此多的基础设施，

sentences.en: I at times worry about the ability of activists to stop things from getting built, you know, transmission lines, other things.
sentences.zh: 有时我会担心激进人士阻挠工程建设的能力，你知道的，比如输电线之类的项目。

sentences.en: And one of the things that I hope people would take away from this book, Phil Tagami at one point says to me, if you brush with Robert Moses, you have to rinse with Jane Jacobs.
sentences.zh: 我希望人们能从这本书里读出一点，菲尔·塔加米曾对我说过：如果你和罗伯特·摩西打过交道，就得用简·雅各布斯来洗洗脑。

sentences.en: Or you could have gotten it the other way.
sentences.zh: 或者反过来也行。

sentences.en: That's a real 99 PI reference there for you.
sentences.zh: 这可是个地道的《99%隐形》梗。

sentences.en: And I kind of feel like it's, wherever you are on the spectrum of like, you know, building stuff, you know, if you're going to brush with Tagami,
sentences.zh: 我觉得，无论你在城市建设这个光谱的哪一端，如果你要和塔加米打交道，

sentences.en: you've got to rinse with Miss Margaret.
sentences.zh: 你就得用玛格丽特女士的观点来平衡一下。

sentences.en: If you're going to brush with Miss Margaret, you've got to, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果你要和玛格丽特女士打交道，你就得，你知道的，

sentences.en: rinse with Tagami because it is fundamentally kind of a different thing to try to build a whole bunch of new stuff, which we do know we actually need to do.
sentences.zh: 用塔加米的观点来平衡一下，因为尝试去建设一大堆新事物，本质上是另一回事，而我们确实知道我们需要这样做。

sentences.en: Like we cannot actually just like freeze everything.
sentences.zh: 我们不可能真的把一切都冻结住。

sentences.en: So for me, it's almost like it's less, you know, like hero and villain, although there's that component to it.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，这与其说是英雄与反派的对立，尽管确实有那样的成分，

sentences.en: And it's more like each of these people contains a piece of what the future world needs to be.
sentences.zh: 不如说每个人都代表了未来世界所需的一部分。

sentences.en: And the thing that must be there is you must actually want good things for the place where you are, which is not, I'm not always sure about that in all cases.
sentences.zh: 最关键的一点是，你必须真心希望你所在的地方变得更好，而这一点，我并不总是能在所有情况下都确定。

sentences.en: But then, you know, people can have different ways of getting to like a good world, you know, and I'm still hoping that Phil gives up on the project and everyone can celebrate.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，人们通往美好世界的路径各不相同，我依然希望菲尔能放弃那个项目，让大家都能皆大欢喜。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So we've talked about, I don't know, like 100 years of Oakland history.
sentences.zh: 所以我们聊了，我不知道，大概一百年的奥克兰历史吧。

sentences.en: How do you think this global economic order that was born right here out of those cranes by the port, how do you think it's changed life in the city?
sentences.zh: 你认为这种诞生于港口起重机之下的全球经济秩序，是如何改变这座城市生活的？

sentences.en: I think to get to, you know, an obvious point about Oakland that must be addressed, it's like Oakland has swapped out a huge percentage of its population for higher income,
sentences.zh: 我认为要谈谈奥克兰一个必须面对的显而易见的事实，那就是奥克兰已经将其很大一部分人口置换成了高收入群体，

sentences.en: less black people.
sentences.zh: 黑人变少了。

sentences.en: And we have really brutal crime still, and now I think demographically shocking the income levels of Oakland relative to its crime rates.
sentences.zh: 我们依然面临着极其残酷的犯罪问题，而且我认为，从人口统计学上看，奥克兰的收入水平与其犯罪率之间的关系令人震惊。

sentences.en: I think people, it's almost like an outlier in that way.
sentences.zh: 我觉得在这一点上，它几乎是个异类。

sentences.en: The city could not gentrify its way to safety, security and vibrancy.
sentences.zh: 这座城市无法通过士绅化来实现安全、稳定和活力。

sentences.en: Instead, we gentrified the hell out of Oakland.
sentences.zh: 相反，我们把奥克兰彻底“士绅化”了。

sentences.en: And there's empty stores everywhere, empty ground floor retail everywhere.
sentences.zh: 到处都是空置的店面，到处都是空置的底层零售空间。

sentences.en: We've got high real estate prices and low everything else.
sentences.zh: 我们有高昂的房地产价格，但其他一切都很低迷。

sentences.en: And it's like, as long as things are market driven in this way, the only thing rich people can do to a place is make the price go up.
sentences.zh: 就像这样，只要一切仍由市场驱动，富人对一个地方唯一能做的就是推高价格。

sentences.en: And I think everyone who lives in poor neighborhoods knows that, which is why gentrification has the name that it does.
sentences.zh: 我想住在贫困社区的人都明白这一点，这就是为什么“士绅化”这个词会有现在的含义。

sentences.en: Even though, I think on its own terms, trying to fight gentrification in the narrow sense by keeping urban change from happening has failed.
sentences.zh: 尽管我认为，就其本身而言，试图通过阻止城市变革来狭隘地对抗士绅化已经失败了。

sentences.en: And you can look around and see the results of that.
sentences.zh: 看看四周，你就能看到结果。

sentences.en: And so I kind of feel like we might be at a bit of like a low point for this, like how we think about what needs to change in cities,
sentences.zh: 所以我感觉我们可能正处于一个低谷期，关于我们如何思考城市需要什么样的变革，

sentences.en: because we're kind of at the end of a line of a bunch of different theories about how to make cities better.
sentences.zh: 因为我们似乎已经走到了各种关于如何让城市变得更好的理论的尽头。

sentences.en: And now we get to try something else.
sentences.zh: 现在我们可以尝试点别的了。

sentences.en: Well, Alexis, thank you so much for talking with me.
sentences.zh: 好的，亚历克西斯，非常感谢你接受我的采访。

sentences.en: Thanks so much for the book.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你的书。

sentences.en: I really enjoyed our conversation.
sentences.zh: 我很享受我们的谈话。

sentences.en: I appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 不客气。

sentences.en: Thank you so much, Roman.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你，罗曼。
